rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Source line 84: "**Read,** Lucas F. da Costa, [Backpressure Is All You Need](https://www.lucasfcosta.com/blog/backpressure-is-all-you-need)** (May 2026)." — a stray unmatched `**` sits right after the link's closing paren, before ' (May 2026).'. Confirmed mechanically: `awk 'NR<=90' <file> | grep -o '**' | wc -l` = 19, an odd count, meaning one `**` in the body has no pair; every other line's `**` pairs cleanly within its own line (checked lines 14-18, 24, 65, 82 all pair). Harm check: §9 exists so bold marks a handle a reader can trust; an unpaired `**` is a markdown-rendering defect, not a budget overage — but it lives in the same emphasis machinery §9 governs and the nearest numbered rule to file it under. Depending on the renderer's pairing scope this either prints literal asterisks on the slide or silently bolds everything from '(May 2026)' onward until the next `**` (none remain in the body, so it would run to end-of-body or into the maintainer block) — either way the slide is not shown as intended. This is a fresh finding: the file's prior-run REVISE on this same rule (both pre-read leads bolding mode-plus-title) is fixed — 'Read,' now bolds alone with the title plain, confirmed at lines 82 and 84 — but the edit that fixed it left this stray delimiter behind.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Delete the stray `**` after the link close-paren on line 84 (or move it to properly wrap '(May 2026)' if bolding the date was intended).
